items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-12-23
items.q: But that band, that Frankie Deuce's band, they had a low band, that's what you call a low band.

ctx.x: Now, what about upstairs? They'd have Robichaud out there, one of those bands.

Robichaud, you know, Imperial Band or Superior, one of those bands, you know what I mean? Well, they played like Maple Leaf Rag and, you know, African Pass and Grayson Buter and, you know, Field Rag, all the tunes, and maybe some popular tunes at that particular time, you know? But that band, that Frankie Deuce's band, they had a low band, that's what you call a low band.
They always hired them to play out in the field.
If you could run through that, do you remember? Yeah, I heard them.

Well, Imperial Band, when I heard them, they had that which was, Manny Paracis, was the lead of that band. And he had Buddy Johnson on trombone at that time. And he had Baby Matthews on drums. And he had George Buckhead on clarinet. And Willie Santiago on the guitar. And Jimmy Brown played the bass. That was Imperial Band. The Superior Band. The Superior Band. Now, pardon me. The Superior Band, in that band, I, when I first seen that band, they had, uh, uh, uh, Mac Murray on drums. They had, uh, Cock and Rumble…
